title: LOTO: Control of Hazardous Energy
body: Every machine that still has hydraulic pressure, electrical charge, or a loaded spring can hurt someone the moment they think it's "just stopped." At ADW, the step that gets skipped under time pressure is always the same one — verification — and that's the step that actually proves the energy is gone.
keyPoints: LOTO applies to any stored or residual energy — electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, thermal, chemical — not just power that's switched on.

Six steps, no shortcuts: prepare, notify, isolate, apply lockout/tagout, release stored energy, verify. Skipping to "isolate and lock" without verifying is how someone gets hurt on equipment everyone assumed was dead.
Personal lock principle: each authorized person applies and holds their own lock. No one else removes it — the person doing the work is the only one who can vouch the isolation is still good.
LOTO is the operational form of LSR 3 (Energy Isolation). A LOTO failure isn't a paperwork miss — it's a defined Life Saving Rule violation.
It's the third layer of the inspection cascade: pre-start catches the obvious, daily inspection catches what's developing, LOTO controls the state while someone's hands are actually in the machine.
apply: Walk the workshop and check locks against whoever's working — if a lock's missing, extra, or someone else's name is on a tag that isn't theirs, that's not a formality gap, that's an open LSR 3 exposure right now.
